se of Representatives Legislative Computer System Study Committee is created. The committee shall be composed of five members of the House of Representatives appointed by the Speaker of the House. The chair and vice chair of the committee shall be elected at the first meeting by the members of the committee. The committee shall study the implementation and effectiveness of the new legislative computer system, known as the Alabama Legislative Information System (ALIS). The committee shall receive input and suggestions from House members, legislative staff, citizens, and other interested parties regarding whether the computer system is effectively and efficiently providing legislative information to the legislative community and the citizens of Alabama. Upon the request of the chair, the Clerk of the House of Representatives shall provide necessary clerical assistance for the work of the committee. The committee shall request the revisions of the ALIS system necessary to efficiently and effectively serve the legislative community. The committee shall stand dissolved and discharged of any further duties and liabilities on adjournment of the 1998 Regular Session. Members of the committee shall not be paid any compensation for their service on the committee. WHEREAS, it is with great pride and pleasure that the Alabama Legislature names the bridge on Corridor X over the Alabama Power Company Rail Line and the Locust Fork of the Black Warrior River near Snowtown, Alabama, in honor of Joe Fuller; and WHEREAS, Mr. Fuller was Chairman of the Corridor X Project for the Birmingham Area Chamber of Commerce and, during his distinguished tenure, was instrumental in raising more than $750,000,000; designing the logo that was used in the project; and purchased bumper stickers to be given out from Birmingham to the Mississippi border at his own expense; now therefore, <<<PAGE 25>>> REGULAR SESSION 2137 27th Day BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the bridge over Corridor X over the Alabama Power Company Rail Line and the Locust Fork of the Black Warrior River near Snowtown, Alabama, be named the Joe Fuller Bridge and that the proper officials are requested to place and maintain markers designating the Joe Fuller Bridge as provided in this resolution. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolution be provided to Joe Fuller as a memento of this honorary designation by the Alabama Legislature. GASOLINE AND MOTOR FUELS FOR ONE YEAR. WHEREAS, the price of regular gasoline is currently averaging approximately $3.65 per gallon and is expected to go to over $4 per gallon this summer; and WHEREAS, the price of diesel fuel is well over $4 per gallon which is greatly impacting the trucking industry; and WHEREAS, consumers and business customers alike are suffering from the high price of gasoline and motor fuel; and WHEREAS, the state currently levies a tax of 16 cents per gallon on gasoline and motor fuels used in this state; and WHEREAS, the federal government is considering the temporary elimination of federal taxes on gasoline and motor fuels; and WHEREAS, if the state tax on gasoline and motor fuels could be removed for a period of time, consumers and business customers could get some relief at the pump; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES OF THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA, That this body urges the Governor to investigate the possibility of removing the state tax on gasoline and motor fuels for one year in order to lower prices at the pump. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolution be forwarded to the Governor and each member of the Alabama Congressional Delegation. On motion of Representative Guin, the resolution, HR700, was adopted. WORD DOWNING OF ANNISTON, ALABAMA. WHEREAS, it is with crushing sorrow that we note the death of Catherine Word Downing, a resident of Anniston, caretaker of the forgotten, newspaper columnist, features editor, mother, wife, dear friend and daughter of the South, on September 4, 2003, at the age of 50 years; and WHEREAS, the Anniston Star has lost its most graceful, car­ ing, and talented writer and its readers have lost a loving voice that embraced everyone from the hills of Cleburne County to the dusty back roads of Clay County; and WHEREAS, all the people of Northeast Alabama and count­ less others from the rest of the state, beyond her borders and beyond the seas who knew her writings have lost a writer who, each week, tossed to them a spirit of being and a celebration of life’s minuet; and WHEREAS, the love and caring friendship evoked in her writings and burned into the memories of anyone who ever read her column will last far beyond the time when the pages of The Anniston Star have crumbled into dust; and WHEREAS, left to cherish the memory of Cathi Downing are not only her beloved husband, R. D.; sons, Will and Louis; daughter, Hanna; and other devoted family members, but also anyone who ever read her column and came to cherish her family almost as their own; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA­ BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we grievously mourn the death of Catherine Word Downing of Anniston, Alabama, and, by copy of this resolution to her husband and children, and to the staff of The Anniston Star for publication to its readers, we extend our heartfelt sympathy and sincere condolence. WHEREAS, recorded with a sense of deep sorrow and loss is the untimely and tragic death of Private First Class Howard Johnson, II, of Mobile, Alabama, who died in action while serving his country with valor in Iraq on March 23, 2003, at the age of 21 years; and WHEREAS, the son of Gloria and Howard Johnson, Sr., PFC Howard Johnson, II, was affectionately known to family and friends as “Junior”; he graduated from LeFlore High School in 2001 and joined the United States Army just two weeks later; and WHEREAS, following his basic training at Fort Jackson, South Carolina, Private Johnson completed his training at Fort Lee in Virginia, specializing as an automated logistical specialist with the 507th Maintenance Company based at Fort Bliss, Texas; and WHEREAS, Howard Johnson was a faithful young member of the Truevine Baptist Church, where his father, the Reverend How­ ard Johnson, is the pastor; he was active in the children’s ministry, in Sunday School, and was always eager to help the elderly people in the church; and WHEREAS, the death of Howard Johnson, II, has indeed left a deep void in the lives of his family, community, and friends who knew him as a fine young man who was focused, goal-oriented, and proud to serve his country in the United States Army, and we give thanks for his life and service; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE SENATE OF ALABAMA, That we hereby honor Private First Class Howard Johnson, II, of Mobile, Alabama, for his service to his country in the War in Iraq, and extend our most heartfelt sympathy to his parents, for whom a copy of this resolution shall be presented that they may know we truly share the sorrow of their great loss. Na- tional Guard has long been recognized for its high military value to the United States of America, effectively and efficiently servicing the state and nation since 1919; and WHEREAS, the 117th Air Refueling Wing continues to im- pressively support our country’s war on terrorism abroad, and its con- tributions are invaluable to the success of these efforts; and <<<PAGE 35>>> 348 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2005 5th Day - July 26, 2005 WHEREAS, the 117th Air Refueling Wing also provides es- sential service to the nation’s homeland defense, advancing proudly and skillfully the long tradition of the Alabama National Guard; and WHEREAS, the Department of Defense has recommended that the 117th Air Refueling Wing lose its KC-135R aircraft to units with less military value, a decision which does not serve the best in- terests of our nation and its citizens; and WHEREAS, federal law prohibits any changes in location of Air National Guard aircraft without the consent of the Governor; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the U.S. Department of Defense recommendations to remove the KC-135R aircraft from the 117th Air Refueling Wing should be rejected and we strongly encourage Alabama’s U.S. Congressional Delegation to take all steps necessary to ensure that these aircraft remain with the Bir- mingham Air Guard Station. Additionally, the task force shall make recommendations on the implementation of a cost- effective plan for early screening, diagnosis, and treatment for the cit- izens of Alabama that are at risk for chronic kidney disease. The task force shall stand dissolved and discharged of any further duties and liabilities on July 1, 2007, unless it is affirmatively renewed before such time.
